paragraphs: R' Sheila. The emperor’s court authorized him to judge, and a miracle was performed for him in the matter of the informer, as recorded in Berakhot [the Warsaw text has גם; the narrative suggests נס]. Above under resh, Heilprin observes that Yuhasin gives the judgeship story to Rabbah bar Sheila too, as if granting the same deed to two parties. The Gemara there, 58a, says: R' Sheila flogged a man who had intercourse with a prostitute. He went and informed the royal court: ‘There is a Jewish man judging without the king's authorization.’ An official was sent for him. When he arrived, they asked, ‘Why did you flog him?’ He answered, ‘Because he had intercourse with a she-ass.’ They asked, ‘Have you witnesses?’ He said yes. Elijah came, appeared as a man, and testified. They said, ‘If so, he is liable to death.’ He said, ‘Since we were exiled, we have no authority to execute,’ etc. While they considered the case, R' Sheila said, ‘Blessed is the Merciful One who gave you rule and love of justice.’ They told him, ‘Since royal honor is important to you, let this man judge all cases.’ They gave him an iron club and told him, ‘Sit at Rome's gate and administer judgment.’ As he left, that man asked him, ‘Does the Merciful One perform miracles for liars?’ He replied, ‘Are they not called asses, as it is written, “Their flesh is the flesh of asses”?’ He wished to go report that he had called them asses. R' Sheila said, ‘This man is a pursuer,’ struck him with the club, and killed him. Gilgulei Neshamot (Yod 6) identifies Yair the Gileadite, the judge, with R' Sheila, and describes him as a spark of Pinhas and the other man as a spark of Zimri. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says in R' Sheila's name.
